hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the assessment underway.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the basics. To check your eligibility, I need to know about the child or children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for.

**First, can you tell me the age of your child?**

- Is your child **under 16 years old**?
- **Between 16 and 19 years old**?
- **20 years old or over**?

Once I know their age, I can guide you through the rest of the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who is 14 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, **Alex, who is 14 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, that's great news as this is one of the qualifying age groups for Child Benefit.

Let me move forward with the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, let me ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

(This check is important because while Alex is under 16, it still affects eligibility. Please let me know about any paid work Alex may be doing.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just in school like any normal 14-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in school and not working, so that's not an issue. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now let me ask about benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)?
- Universal Credit?

(These are benefits that, if received directly by the child, would affect eligibility. Is Alex receiving any of these?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just 14, so they wouldn't be getting anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship programme?**

Since Alex is 14 and in school, they're likely not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm. If they are, the rules vary by region (England, Scotland, and Wales have different rules about which apprenticeships affect eligibility).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any apprenticeship. They're just doing regular school work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is just in regular school, so that's not an issue. Let me move to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check your residency situation, which is an important part of Child Benefit eligibility:

**Which of the following best describes your situation?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most common situation
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you're an EU citizen who settled before certain dates
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - which might involve working, jobseeking, studying, having sufficient resources, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
4. **You're a Crown servant (such as a diplomat) living abroad or in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't live in the UK actually. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you're living abroad, let me ask a bit more to understand your specific situation:

**Can you tell me which of the following applies to you?**

1. **Are you a Crown servant** (such as a diplomat or civil servant) living abroad as part of your official duties?

2. **Or are you living abroad in some other capacity** (such as for work, family reasons, etc.)?

This will help me determine if there are any special circumstances that might still allow you to claim Child Benefit while living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad for personal reasons.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit** because you don't meet the residency requirements.

Here's why:

**Residency Requirement:**
To claim Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. The only exceptions are:
- If you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- If you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme and meet certain specific conditions (working, jobseeking, studying, etc.)
- If you're a Crown servant living abroad in certain circumstances

Since you're living abroad for personal reasons and don't fall into any of these special categories, you unfortunately don't meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**What you might want to do:**

- If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK in the future, you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that point
- You may want to contact HMRC directly to discuss your specific situation, as there may be nuances I'm not aware of: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about the eligibility rules?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. No, I think you've explained it clearly - I need to be living in the UK to claim. Thank you for checking that for me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you, even though it's disappointing news. You've understood it correctly – the UK residency requirement is a key part of Child Benefit eligibility.

If your circumstances change in the future and you do move back to the UK, please feel free to come back and we can run through the assessment again. At that point, with Alex still being a qualifying age, you'd be in a much stronger position to claim.

Best of luck, and if you have any other questions in the future, don't hesitate to ask!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Take care!
